passages.text: After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream: He was standing beside the Nile, when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Two years passed after Joseph interpreted dreams in prison.
Pharaoh had a dream.
In his dream, Pharaoh stood beside the Nile River.
Seven cows came up from the river.
These cows looked beautiful.
These cows were healthy and well-fed.
The seven cows began to graze among the reeds.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ שְׁנָתַ֣יִם יָמִ֑ים וּפַרְעֹ֣ה חֹלֵ֔ם וְהִנֵּ֖ה עֹמֵ֥ד עַל־ הַיְאֹֽר׃ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִן־ הַיְאֹ֗ר עֹלֹת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פָּר֔וֹת יְפ֥וֹת מַרְאֶ֖ה וּבְרִיאֹ֣ת בָּשָׂ֑ר וַתִּרְעֶ֖ינָה בָּאָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: After them, seven other cows, sickly and thin, came up from the Nile and stood beside the well-fed cows on the bank of the river.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh had a dream.
In his dream, he stood by the Nile River.
Seven cows came up from the river.
These cows were sickly and thin.
They came up after the first cows.
The sickly, thin cows stood beside the well-fed cows.
They stood together on the bank of the river.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶׁ֧בַע פָּר֣וֹת אֲחֵר֗וֹת עֹל֤וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶן֙ מִן־ הַיְאֹ֔ר רָע֥וֹת מַרְאֶ֖ה וְדַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֛דְנָה אֵ֥צֶל הַפָּר֖וֹת עַל־ שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃

passages.text: And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows. Then Pharaoh woke up, but he fell back asleep and dreamed a second time: Seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, came up on one stalk.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh had a dream at night.
In his dream, seven cows appeared.
These cows looked sickly and thin.
The sickly, thin cows ate seven other cows.
The other cows looked sleek and well-fed.
Pharaoh woke up from his dream.
Pharaoh went back to sleep.
He dreamed a second time.
In the second dream, seven heads of grain appeared.
These heads of grain were plump and ripe.
All seven heads of grain grew on one stalk.
passages.original: וַתֹּאכַ֣לְנָה הַפָּר֗וֹת רָע֤וֹת הַמַּרְאֶה֙ וְדַקֹּ֣ת הַבָּשָׂ֔ר אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַפָּר֔וֹת יְפֹ֥ת הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְהַבְּרִיאֹ֑ת וַיִּיקַ֖ץ פַּרְעֹֽה׃ וַיִּישָׁ֕ן וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֖ם שֵׁנִ֑ית וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹל֛וֹת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד בְּרִיא֥וֹת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted, thin and scorched by the east wind.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh had a dream.
In his dream, he saw heads of grain.
Seven heads of grain appeared after the first ones.
These seven heads of grain were thin.
The seven heads of grain were scorched by the east wind.
The seven thin, scorched heads of grain sprouted after the others.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים דַּקּ֖וֹת וּשְׁדוּפֹ֣ת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽן׃

passages.text: And the thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven plump, ripe ones. Then Pharaoh awoke and realized it was a dream.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh saw a dream.
In the dream, there were heads of grain.
Seven heads of grain were thin.
Seven heads of grain were plump and full.
The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump, full heads of grain.
Pharaoh woke up.
Pharaoh realized it was a dream.
passages.original: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְנָה֙ הַשִּׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקּ֔וֹת אֵ֚ת שֶׁ֣בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִ֔ים הַבְּרִיא֖וֹת וְהַמְּלֵא֑וֹת וַיִּיקַ֥ץ פַּרְעֹ֖ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֲלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: In the morning his spirit was troubled, so he summoned all the magicians and wise men of Egypt. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but no one could interpret them for him.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
In the morning, Pharaoh felt troubled in his spirit.
He called for all the magicians of Egypt.
He also called for all the wise men of Egypt.
Pharaoh told his dreams to these men.
No one could interpret the dreams for Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֙קֶר֙ וַתִּפָּ֣עֶם רוּח֔וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֗ח וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־ כָּל־ חַרְטֻמֵּ֥י מִצְרַ֖יִם וְאֶת־ כָּל־ חֲכָמֶ֑יהָ וַיְסַפֵּ֨ר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לָהֶם֙ אֶת־ חֲלֹמ֔וֹ וְאֵין־ פּוֹתֵ֥ר אוֹתָ֖ם לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Then the chief cupbearer said to Pharaoh, “Today I recall my failures.
passages.sermon: The chief cupbearer spoke to Pharaoh.\r\nHe said, “Today I remember my wrongdoings.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַמַּשְׁקִ֔ים אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֶת־ חֲטָאַ֕י אֲנִ֖י מַזְכִּ֥יר הַיּֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Pharaoh was once angry with his servants, and he put me and the chief baker in the custody of the captain of the guard.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh became angry with his servants.
Pharaoh punished us.
Pharaoh put me in custody.
Pharaoh put the chief baker in custody.
The captain of the guard watched over us.
passages.original: פַּרְעֹ֖ה קָצַ֣ף עַל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו וַיִּתֵּ֨ן אֹתִ֜י בְּמִשְׁמַ֗ר בֵּ֚ית שַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים אֹתִ֕י וְאֵ֖ת שַׂ֥ר הָאֹפִֽים׃

passages.text: One night both the chief baker and I had dreams, and each dream had its own meaning.
passages.sermon:
The chief cupbearer and the chief baker were both in prison together.
One night, we each had a dream.
Each dream was different.
Each dream had its own meaning.
passages.original: וַנַּֽחַלְמָ֥ה חֲל֛וֹם בְּלַ֥יְלָה אֶחָ֖ד אֲנִ֣י וָה֑וּא אִ֛ישׁ כְּפִתְר֥וֹן חֲלֹמ֖וֹ חָלָֽמְנוּ׃

passages.text: Now a young Hebrew was there with us, a servant of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams and he interpreted them for us individually.
passages.sermon:
A young Hebrew was with us in prison.
He was a servant of the captain of the guard.
We told him our dreams.
He listened to each dream.
He interpreted each dream for us.
He gave each man the meaning of his own dream.
passages.original: וְשָׁ֨ם אִתָּ֜נוּ נַ֣עַר עִבְרִ֗י עֶ֚בֶד לְשַׂ֣ר הַטַּבָּחִ֔ים וַנְּ֨סַפֶּר־ ל֔וֹ וַיִּפְתָּר־ לָ֖נוּ אֶת־ חֲלֹמֹתֵ֑ינוּ אִ֥ישׁ כַּחֲלֹמ֖וֹ פָּתָֽר׃

passages.text: And it happened to us just as he had interpreted: I was restored to my position, and the other man was hanged.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a young Hebrew.
He was a servant of the captain of the guard.
He interpreted our dreams for us.
He gave each of us the meaning of our dream.
Everything happened just as Joseph said.
I was restored to my position.
The other man was hanged.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר פָּֽתַר־ לָ֖נוּ כֵּ֣ן הָיָ֑ה אֹתִ֛י הֵשִׁ֥יב עַל־ כַּנִּ֖י וְאֹת֥וֹ תָלָֽה׃

passages.text: So Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of the dungeon. After he had shaved and changed his clothes, he went in before Pharaoh.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
Joseph was in prison.
Pharaoh sent messengers to Joseph.
The messengers called Joseph to come.
They brought Joseph quickly out of the prison.
Joseph shaved himself.
Joseph changed his clothes.
Joseph went in to see Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח פַּרְעֹה֙ וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶת־ יוֹסֵ֔ף וַיְרִיצֻ֖הוּ מִן־ הַבּ֑וֹר וַיְגַלַּח֙ וַיְחַלֵּ֣ף שִׂמְלֹתָ֔יו וַיָּבֹ֖א אֶל־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I had a dream, and no one can interpret it. But I have heard it said of you that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “I had a dream.
No one can explain my dream.
I heard something about you.
People say you can hear a dream.
People say you can explain a dream.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף חֲל֣וֹם חָלַ֔מְתִּי וּפֹתֵ֖ר אֵ֣ין אֹת֑וֹ וַאֲנִ֗י שָׁמַ֤עְתִּי עָלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר תִּשְׁמַ֥ע חֲל֖וֹם לִפְתֹּ֥ר אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: “I myself cannot do it,” Joseph replied, “but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph stood before Pharaoh.
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
Joseph had been brought from prison to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh asked Joseph to interpret his dream.
Joseph answered Pharaoh.
Joseph said, “I cannot do it by myself.”
Joseph said, “God will give Pharaoh the answer.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן יוֹסֵ֧ף אֶת־ פַּרְעֹ֛ה לֵאמֹ֖ר בִּלְעָדָ֑י אֱלֹהִ֕ים יַעֲנֶ֖ה אֶת־ שְׁל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph: “In my dream I was standing on the bank of the Nile, when seven cows, well-fed and sleek, came up from the river and began to graze among the reeds.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh described his dream to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “In my dream, I stood on the bank of the Nile River.
I saw seven cows come up from the river.
These cows were healthy and strong.
These cows looked beautiful.
The seven cows began to eat grass among the reeds.”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֑ף בַּחֲלֹמִ֕י הִנְנִ֥י עֹמֵ֖ד עַל־ שְׂפַ֥ת הַיְאֹֽר׃ וְהִנֵּ֣ה מִן־ הַיְאֹ֗ר עֹלֹת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע פָּר֔וֹת בְּרִיא֥וֹת בָּשָׂ֖ר וִיפֹ֣ת תֹּ֑אַר וַתִּרְעֶ֖ינָה בָּאָֽחוּ׃

passages.text: After them, seven other cows—sickly, ugly, and thin—came up. I have never seen such ugly cows in all the land of Egypt!
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph about his dream.
Pharaoh saw seven other cows come up after the first cows.
These seven cows looked sickly.
These cows looked very ugly.
These cows were thin.
Pharaoh had never seen cows as ugly as these in all the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּ֞ה שֶֽׁבַע־ פָּר֤וֹת אֲחֵרוֹת֙ עֹל֣וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן דַּלּ֨וֹת וְרָע֥וֹת תֹּ֛אַר מְאֹ֖ד וְרַקּ֣וֹת בָּשָׂ֑ר לֹֽא־ רָאִ֧יתִי כָהֵ֛נָּה בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לָרֹֽעַ׃

passages.text: Then the thin, ugly cows devoured the seven well-fed cows that were there first.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh had a dream.
Pharaoh saw cows in his dream.
Seven cows were thin and ugly.
Seven cows were well-fed and healthy.
The thin, ugly cows ate the seven well-fed cows.
The well-fed cows were the first ones there.
passages.original: וַתֹּאכַ֙לְנָה֙ הַפָּר֔וֹת הָרַקּ֖וֹת וְהָרָע֑וֹת אֵ֣ת שֶׁ֧בַע הַפָּר֛וֹת הָרִאשֹׁנ֖וֹת הַבְּרִיאֹֽת׃

passages.text: When they had devoured them, however, no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before. Then I awoke.
passages.sermon:
Seven thin, ugly cows ate the seven healthy cows.
No one could tell that the thin cows had eaten the healthy cows.
The thin cows still looked just as ugly as before.
I woke up.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֣אנָה אֶל־ קִרְבֶּ֗נָה וְלֹ֤א נוֹדַע֙ כִּי־ בָ֣אוּ אֶל־ קִרְבֶּ֔נָה וּמַרְאֵיהֶ֣ן רַ֔ע כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר בַּתְּחִלָּ֑ה וָאִיקָֽץ׃

passages.text: In my dream I also saw seven heads of grain, plump and ripe, growing on a single stalk.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh had a dream.
\r\nIn the dream, Pharaoh saw seven heads of grain.
\r\nThe seven heads of grain grew on one stalk.
\r\nThe seven heads of grain were full.
\r\nThe seven heads of grain were good.
passages.original: וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲלֹמִ֑י וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֗ים עֹלֹ֛ת בְּקָנֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד מְלֵאֹ֥ת וְטֹבֽוֹת׃

passages.text: After them, seven other heads of grain sprouted—withered, thin, and scorched by the east wind.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh had a dream.
\r\nIn his dream, he saw heads of grain.
\r\nSeven heads of grain appeared after the first ones.
\r\nThese seven heads of grain looked withered.
\r\nThey were thin.
\r\nThe east wind had scorched them.
\r\nThey grew up after the good heads of grain.
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שִׁבֳּלִ֔ים צְנֻמ֥וֹת דַּקּ֖וֹת שְׁדֻפ֣וֹת קָדִ֑ים צֹמְח֖וֹת אַחֲרֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: And the thin heads of grain swallowed the seven plump ones. I told this dream to the magicians, but no one could explain it to me.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh had a dream.
In the dream, seven thin heads of grain appeared.
These thin heads of grain swallowed seven plump heads of grain.
Pharaoh told this dream to the magicians.
None of the magicians could explain the dream to Pharaoh.
passages.original: וַתִּבְלַ֙עְןָ֙ הָשִׁבֳּלִ֣ים הַדַּקֹּ֔ת אֵ֛ת שֶׁ֥בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִ֖ים הַטֹּב֑וֹת וָֽאֹמַר֙ אֶל־ הַֽחַרְטֻמִּ֔ים וְאֵ֥ין מַגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

passages.text: At this, Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dreams of Pharaoh are one and the same. God has revealed to Pharaoh what He is about to do.
passages.sermon:
Joseph stood before Pharaoh.
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh.
Pharaoh had dreams.
The dreams are one and the same.
God revealed something to Pharaoh.
God showed Pharaoh what He is about to do.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יוֹסֵף֙ אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֔ה חֲל֥וֹם פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶחָ֣ד ה֑וּא אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הִגִּ֥יד לְפַרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: The seven good cows are seven years, and the seven ripe heads of grain are seven years. The dreams have the same meaning.
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh.
Joseph explained Pharaoh’s dream.
The seven good cows mean seven years.
The seven good heads of grain also mean seven years.
Both dreams have the same meaning.
passages.original: שֶׁ֧בַע פָּרֹ֣ת הַטֹּבֹ֗ת שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִּׁבֳּלִים֙ הַטֹּבֹ֔ת שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים הֵ֑נָּה חֲל֖וֹם אֶחָ֥ד הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Moreover, the seven thin, ugly cows that came up after them are seven years, and so are the seven worthless heads of grain scorched by the east wind—they are seven years of famine.
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh.
Joseph explained the meaning of Pharaoh’s dream.
Seven thin cows appeared after the good cows.
These seven thin cows represent seven years.
Seven ugly cows also appeared.
These ugly cows also represent seven years.
Seven empty heads of grain appeared.
The east wind scorched these heads of grain.
These empty heads of grain also represent seven years.
All these things mean seven years of famine will come.
passages.original: וְשֶׁ֣בַע הַ֠פָּרוֹת הָֽרַקּ֨וֹת וְהָרָעֹ֜ת הָעֹלֹ֣ת אַחֲרֵיהֶ֗ן שֶׁ֤בַע שָׁנִים֙ הֵ֔נָּה וְשֶׁ֤בַע הַֽשִׁבֳּלִים֙ הָרֵק֔וֹת שְׁדֻפ֖וֹת הַקָּדִ֑ים יִהְי֕וּ שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י רָעָֽב׃

passages.text: It is just as I said to Pharaoh: God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh.
Joseph explained the meaning of Pharaoh’s dreams.
Joseph said, “This is what I told you, Pharaoh.”
God is acting.
God has shown Pharaoh what He is about to do.
passages.original: ה֣וּא הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים עֹשֶׂ֖ה הֶרְאָ֥ה אֶת־ פַּרְעֹֽה׃

passages.text: Behold, seven years of great abundance are coming throughout the land of Egypt, but seven years of famine will follow them. Then all the abundance in the land of Egypt will be forgotten, and the famine will devastate the land.
passages.sermon:
Egypt is the land in this passage.
Seven years will come.
These seven years will bring great abundance.
All of Egypt will have plenty during these years.
After these seven years, another period will begin.
Seven years of famine will follow.
People will forget all the abundance in Egypt.
The famine will destroy the land.
passages.original: הִנֵּ֛ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים בָּא֑וֹת שָׂבָ֥ע גָּד֖וֹל בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ וְ֠קָמוּ שֶׁ֜בַע שְׁנֵ֤י רָעָב֙ אַחֲרֵיהֶ֔ן וְנִשְׁכַּ֥ח כָּל־ הַשָּׂבָ֖ע בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְכִלָּ֥ה הָרָעָ֖ב אֶת־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: The abundance in the land will not be remembered, since the famine that follows it will be so severe.
passages.sermon:
A famine will come after the years of abundance in Egypt.
This famine will be very severe.
People will not remember the abundance in the land.
The famine will be so harsh that it will make everyone forget the good years.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ יִוָּדַ֤ע הַשָּׂבָע֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִפְּנֵ֛י הָרָעָ֥ב הַה֖וּא אַחֲרֵי־ כֵ֑ן כִּֽי־ כָבֵ֥ד ה֖וּא מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: Moreover, because the dream was given to Pharaoh in two versions, the matter has been decreed by God, and He will carry it out shortly.
passages.sermon:
God gave Pharaoh a dream.
God gave the dream to Pharaoh two times.
God decided what will happen.
God will do it soon.
passages.original: וְעַ֨ל הִשָּׁנ֧וֹת הַחֲל֛וֹם אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֖ה פַּעֲמָ֑יִם כִּֽי־ נָכ֤וֹן הַדָּבָר֙ מֵעִ֣ם הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וּמְמַהֵ֥ר הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לַעֲשֹׂתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now, therefore, Pharaoh should look for a discerning and wise man and set him over the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh is the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh should find a man who is discerning.
Pharaoh should find a man who is wise.
Pharaoh should appoint this man over the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ יֵרֶ֣א פַרְעֹ֔ה אִ֖ישׁ נָב֣וֹן וְחָכָ֑ם וִישִׁיתֵ֖הוּ עַל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Let Pharaoh take action and appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh is the ruler of Egypt.
Pharaoh should act now.
Pharaoh should appoint officials over the land.
These officials will collect a fifth of the harvest from Egypt.
They will do this during the seven years of abundance.
passages.original: יַעֲשֶׂ֣ה פַרְעֹ֔ה וְיַפְקֵ֥ד פְּקִדִ֖ים עַל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ וְחִמֵּשׁ֙ אֶת־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֥י הַשָּׂבָֽע׃

passages.text: Under the authority of Pharaoh, let them collect all the excess food from these good years, that they may come and lay up the grain to be preserved as food in the cities.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh rules Egypt.
Pharaoh has authority over the land.
Let Pharaoh’s appointed men collect all the extra food.
The extra food comes from the good years.
Let them gather the grain.
Let them store the grain under Pharaoh’s control.
Let them keep the food in the cities.
Let them preserve the food for the future.
passages.original: וְיִקְבְּצ֗וּ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֹ֙כֶל֙ הַשָּׁנִ֣ים הַטֹּבֹ֔ת הַבָּאֹ֖ת הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְיִצְבְּרוּ־ בָ֞ר תַּ֧חַת יַד־ פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֹ֥כֶל בֶּעָרִ֖ים וְשָׁמָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: This food will be a reserve for the land during the seven years of famine to come upon the land of Egypt. Then the country will not perish in the famine.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph spoke to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.
Joseph said there would be seven years of famine in Egypt.
He said to store food as a reserve for the land.
This food would be kept for the seven years of famine.
The famine would come upon the land of Egypt.
The stored food would keep the country alive.
The land would not perish in the famine.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֨ה הָאֹ֤כֶל לְפִקָּדוֹן֙ לָאָ֔רֶץ לְשֶׁ֙בַע֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הָרָעָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּהְיֶ֖יןָ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹֽא־ תִכָּרֵ֥ת הָאָ֖רֶץ בָּרָעָֽב׃

passages.text: This proposal pleased Pharaoh and all his officials.
passages.sermon: Pharaoh heard the proposal.\r\nPharaoh felt pleased.\r\nAll Pharaoh’s officials also felt pleased.
passages.original: וַיִּיטַ֥ב הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־ עֲבָדָֽיו׃

passages.text: So Pharaoh asked them, “Can we find anyone like this man, in whom the Spirit of God abides?”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to his officials.
Pharaoh asked a question.
Pharaoh said, “Can we find anyone like this man?”
Pharaoh meant Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “This man has the Spirit of God in him.”
Pharaoh saw that Joseph was special because God’s Spirit was with him.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֑יו הֲנִמְצָ֣א כָזֶ֔ה אִ֕ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֛ר ר֥וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Since God has made all this known to you, there is no one as discerning and wise as you.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
God had revealed important things to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “God has shown you all these things.”
Pharaoh said, “No one is as discerning as you.”
Pharaoh said, “No one is as wise as you.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר פַּרְעֹה֙ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אַחֲרֵ֨י הוֹדִ֧יעַ אֱלֹהִ֛ים אוֹתְךָ֖ אֶת־ כָּל־ זֹ֑את אֵין־ נָב֥וֹן וְחָכָ֖ם כָּמֽוֹךָ׃

passages.text: You shall be in charge of my house, and all my people are to obey your commands. Only with regard to the throne will I be greater than you.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
Pharaoh said, “You will be in charge of my house.
All my people will obey your commands.
I will be greater than you only in the throne.
In every other way, you will have authority over my house and my people.”
passages.original: אַתָּה֙ תִּהְיֶ֣ה עַל־ בֵּיתִ֔י וְעַל־ פִּ֖יךָ יִשַּׁ֣ק כָּל־ עַמִּ֑י רַ֥ק הַכִּסֵּ֖א אֶגְדַּ֥ל מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Pharaoh also told Joseph, “I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “Look, I have given you authority.
I have put you in charge of all the land of Egypt.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֖ה אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֑ף רְאֵה֙ נָתַ֣תִּי אֹֽתְךָ֔ עַ֖ל כָּל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger, clothed him in garments of fine linen, and placed a gold chain around his neck.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh took his signet ring off his own hand.
Pharaoh put the signet ring on Joseph’s hand.
Pharaoh dressed Joseph in fine linen clothes.
Pharaoh put a gold chain around Joseph’s neck.
passages.original: וַיָּ֨סַר פַּרְעֹ֤ה אֶת־ טַבַּעְתּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל יָד֔וֹ וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֖הּ עַל־ יַ֣ד יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתוֹ֙ בִּגְדֵי־ שֵׁ֔שׁ וַיָּ֛שֶׂם רְבִ֥ד הַזָּהָ֖ב עַל־ צַוָּארֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He had Joseph ride in his second chariot, with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!” So he placed him over all the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh ruled Egypt.
\r\nPharaoh chose Joseph to rule under him.
\r\nPharaoh gave Joseph great authority.
\r\nPharaoh made Joseph ride in his second chariot.
\r\nMen went before Joseph.
\r\nThe men called out, “Bow the knee!”
\r\nPharaoh placed Joseph over all the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיַּרְכֵּ֣ב אֹת֗וֹ בְּמִרְכֶּ֤בֶת הַמִּשְׁנֶה֙ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְרְא֥וּ לְפָנָ֖יו אַבְרֵ֑ךְ וְנָת֣וֹן אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל כָּל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And Pharaoh declared to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh, but without your permission, no one in all the land of Egypt shall lift his hand or foot.”
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to Joseph.
Pharaoh said, “I am Pharaoh.”
Pharaoh said, “No one in all the land of Egypt will move a hand or a foot without your permission.”
Pharaoh gave Joseph authority over all Egypt.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֛ה אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֖ף אֲנִ֣י פַרְעֹ֑ה וּבִלְעָדֶ֗יךָ לֹֽא־ יָרִ֨ים אִ֧ישׁ אֶת־ יָד֛וֹ וְאֶת־ רַגְל֖וֹ בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah, and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife. And Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Pharaoh gave Joseph a new name.
Pharaoh called Joseph Zaphenath-paneah.
Pharaoh gave Joseph a wife.
Joseph’s wife was Asenath.
Asenath was the daughter of Potiphera.
Potiphera was a priest of On.
Joseph became the ruler over all the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֨א פַרְעֹ֣ה שֵׁם־ יוֹסֵף֮ צָֽפְנַ֣ת פַּעְנֵחַ֒ וַיִּתֶּן־ ל֣וֹ אֶת־ אָֽסְנַ֗ת בַּת־ פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֛רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֹ֖ן לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיֵּצֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֖ף עַל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt. And Joseph left Pharaoh’s presence and traveled throughout the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was thirty years old.
Joseph stood before Pharaoh.
Pharaoh was the king of Egypt.
Joseph left Pharaoh’s presence.
Joseph traveled through all the land of Egypt.
passages.original: וְיוֹסֵף֙ בֶּן־ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה בְּעָמְד֕וֹ לִפְנֵ֖י פַּרְעֹ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיֵּצֵ֤א יוֹסֵף֙ מִלִּפְנֵ֣י פַרְעֹ֔ה וַֽיַּעְבֹ֖ר בְּכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: During the seven years of abundance, the land brought forth bountifully.
passages.sermon: The land of Egypt produced much food.\r\nThis happened during seven years of abundance.\r\nThe land gave plentiful harvests.
passages.original: וַתַּ֣עַשׂ הָאָ֔רֶץ בְּשֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע לִקְמָצִֽים׃

passages.text: During those seven years, Joseph collected all the excess food in the land of Egypt and stored it in the cities. In every city he laid up the food from the fields around it.
passages.sermon:
Joseph served Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
Joseph acted during seven years of abundance in Egypt.
Joseph collected all the extra food from those seven years.
He gathered this food from the whole land of Egypt.
Joseph stored the food in the cities.
He put the food from each city’s surrounding fields into that city.
passages.original: וַיִּקְבֹּ֞ץ אֶת־ כָּל־ אֹ֣כֶל׀ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָיוּ֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּתֶּן־ אֹ֖כֶל בֶּעָרִ֑ים אֹ֧כֶל שְׂדֵה־ הָעִ֛יר אֲשֶׁ֥ר סְבִיבֹתֶ֖יהָ נָתַ֥ן בְּתוֹכָֽהּ׃

passages.text: So Joseph stored up grain in such abundance, like the sand of the sea, that he stopped keeping track of it; for it was beyond measure.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was the governor in Egypt.
Joseph stored grain.
He gathered a very large amount of grain.
The grain was as plentiful as the sand by the sea.
Joseph stored so much grain that he stopped counting it.
No one could measure the amount of grain.
passages.original: וַיִּצְבֹּ֨ר יוֹסֵ֥ף בָּ֛ר כְּח֥וֹל הַיָּ֖ם הַרְבֵּ֣ה מְאֹ֑ד עַ֛ד כִּי־ חָדַ֥ל לִסְפֹּ֖ר כִּי־ אֵ֥ין מִסְפָּֽר׃

passages.text: Before the years of famine arrived, two sons were born to Joseph by Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On.
passages.sermon:
Joseph lived in Egypt.
Joseph served as a leader in Egypt.
Before the years of famine came, Joseph had two sons.
Asenath was Joseph’s wife.
Asenath was the daughter of Potiphera.
Potiphera was a priest of On.
Asenath gave birth to Joseph’s two sons.
passages.original: וּלְיוֹסֵ֤ף יֻלַּד֙ שְׁנֵ֣י בָנִ֔ים בְּטֶ֥רֶם תָּב֖וֹא שְׁנַ֣ת הָרָעָ֑ב אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָֽלְדָה־ לּוֹ֙ אָֽסְנַ֔ת בַּת־ פּ֥וֹטִי פֶ֖רַע כֹּהֵ֥ן אֽוֹן׃

passages.text: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, “God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father’s household.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a Hebrew man.
Joseph lived in Egypt.
Joseph had a first son.
Joseph named his first son Manasseh.
Joseph said, “God has made me forget all my hardship.”
Joseph said, “God has made me forget all my father’s household.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־ שֵׁ֥ם הַבְּכ֖וֹר מְנַשֶּׁ֑ה כִּֽי־ נַשַּׁ֤נִי אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ עֲמָלִ֔י וְאֵ֖ת כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: And the second son he named Ephraim, saying, “God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”
passages.sermon:
Joseph was a ruler in Egypt.
\r\nJoseph had two sons.
\r\nJoseph named his second son Ephraim.
\r\nJoseph said, “God made me fruitful.”
\r\nJoseph lived in a land where he suffered.
\r\nGod made Joseph fruitful in that land of suffering.
passages.original: וְאֵ֛ת שֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖י קָרָ֣א אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּֽי־ הִפְרַ֥נִי אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּאֶ֥רֶץ עָנְיִֽי׃

passages.text: When the seven years of abundance in the land of Egypt came to an end, the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. And although there was famine in every country, there was food throughout the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
Joseph was in Egypt.
God gave Egypt seven years of abundance.
These seven years ended.
Then seven years of famine began.
Joseph had predicted this famine.
Famine came to every country.
But Egypt still had food.
passages.original: וַתִּכְלֶ֕ינָה שֶׁ֖בַע שְׁנֵ֣י הַשָּׂבָ֑ע אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃ וַתְּחִלֶּ֜ינָה שֶׁ֣בַע שְׁנֵ֤י הָרָעָב֙ לָב֔וֹא כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אָמַ֣ר יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בְּכָל־ הָ֣אֲרָצ֔וֹת וּבְכָל־ אֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם הָ֥יָה לָֽחֶם׃

passages.text: When extreme hunger came to all the land of Egypt and the people cried out to Pharaoh for food, he told all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph and do whatever he tells you.”
passages.sermon:
Extreme hunger came to all the land of Egypt.
The people of Egypt became very hungry.
The people cried out to Pharaoh for food.
Pharaoh was the ruler of Egypt.
Pharaoh spoke to all the Egyptians.
Pharaoh said, “Go to Joseph.”
Joseph was in charge of the food in Egypt.
Pharaoh said, “Do whatever Joseph tells you.”
passages.original: וַתִּרְעַב֙ כָּל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וַיִּצְעַ֥ק הָעָ֛ם אֶל־ פַּרְעֹ֖ה לַלָּ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֨אמֶר פַּרְעֹ֤ה לְכָל־ מִצְרַ֙יִם֙ לְכ֣וּ אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֔ף אֲשֶׁר־ יֹאמַ֥ר לָכֶ֖ם תַּעֲשֽׂוּ׃

passages.text: When the famine had spread over all the land, Joseph opened up all the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians; for the famine was severe in the land of Egypt.
passages.sermon:
A famine covered the whole land.
Joseph was in charge in Egypt.
Joseph opened all the storehouses.
Joseph sold grain to the Egyptians.
The famine was very severe in Egypt.
passages.original: וְהָרָעָ֣ב הָיָ֔ה עַ֖ל כָּל־ פְּנֵ֣י הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּפְתַּ֨ח יוֹסֵ֜ף אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר בָּהֶם֙ וַיִּשְׁבֹּ֣ר לְמִצְרַ֔יִם וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָֽרָעָ֖ב בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was severe over all the earth.
passages.sermon:
A severe famine struck all the earth.
People everywhere suffered from hunger.
Joseph was in Egypt.
Joseph managed the grain supplies in Egypt.
People from every nation traveled to Egypt.
They came to Joseph to buy grain.
They did this because the famine was very strong everywhere.
passages.original: וְכָל־ הָאָ֙רֶץ֙ בָּ֣אוּ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה לִשְׁבֹּ֖ר אֶל־ יוֹסֵ֑ף כִּֽי־ חָזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בְּכָל־ הָאָֽרֶץ׃
